subject: VaultBank: urgent - reserved throughput divergence causing high-latency & 5xx
messages:
From: Chris Mercer <chris.mercer@vaultbank.com>
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Persistent latency + 5xx during peak - reserved throughput shortfall

Hi Naomi —

We started seeing a sustained latency increase (~300-600ms p95 to 1.8s p95) and a spike in 5xx errors around 08:45 PDT during the morning business window. Our telemetry shows our reserved throughput consumption hit the ceiling and requests started queueing, then some started failing with 5xx. Attaching a short graph and a CSV of sampled errors.

Impact: customer-facing ML feature (document ingestion) saw ~12% failed requests, and SLA alerting fired. This is impacting a small set of accounts but is visible in production.

Can Redwood confirm whether this is an internal serving regression or if our reserved capacity was misapplied? We need immediate remediation and a short-term mitigation plan.

Chris Mercer
SRE, VaultBank
Attachment: vaultbank_latency_graph.png (png)
Attachment: escalation_metrics_20270807.csv (csv)

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-07T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Persistent latency + 5xx during peak - reserved throughput shortfall

Folks — forwarding an urgent customer report from VaultBank. Internal participants only: Karthik (serving/runtime), Irene (ops), Aditya (accounts/procurement). Marissa for visibility.

What I need in the next 30m:
- Quick root cause triage (is this reserved-capacity enforcement, scheduling, or kernel regression?)
- Immediate mitigations we can apply without breaking VaultBank: temporary burst, lowering model variant, or routing fallback.
- Short note I can send back to the customer summarizing actions + ETA.

I have attached the customer graphs. I also need a recommendation on whether we should pre-authorize a short paid burst (they're out of contract burst) or provide a credit.

- Naomi
VP, Account Ops
Redwood Inference
Attachments: vaultbank_latency_graph.png, escalation_metrics_20270807.csv

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-07T09:41:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Persistent latency + 5xx during peak - reserved throughput shortfall

Quick triage: I've pulled the routing logs and reservation allocations for VaultBank's Dedicated pool. Two observations: (1) Their reserved allocation shows at capacity on the headroom meter starting 08:30 PDT; (2) We had an autoscaling churn event in the same window where a recent internal canary (non-customer workload) briefly consumed GPU slots due to a mis-tagged queue.

Immediate mitigations I can execute now (ETA 15m):
- Evict non-critical canary jobs from the affected nodes and pause preemptible workloads.
- Apply a transient routing rule to route 25% of VaultBank's requests to a compatible lower-throughput model (quantized variant) for 1 hour.
- Enable KV-prefix caching for repeated prefixes where applicable (should shave p95 by 250-450ms for many calls).

Constraints: the transient routing + model fallback will reduce per-request quality slightly; need customer sign-off for fallback. Evicting canaries is safe and I can start that immediately.

I'll start evictions and follow up in 10m with updated headroom numbers.

- Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: irene_choi@redwood.com
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-07T09:53:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Persistent latency + 5xx during peak - reserved throughput shortfall

Started the evictions at 09:50 PDT. Non-critical canaries drained from the dedicated nodes and preemptible queues paused. Current headroom improved by ~14% (tracking in ops dashboard).

I'm requesting emergency burst authorization: +20% reserved throughput for 2 hours to cover peak until we can complete fallback routing and prefix caching. If exec authorization isn't available immediately we'll still hold the evictions and enable the routing fallback.

Also attaching a short infra dump for traces I captured: rb_infra_dump_20270807.tar.gz (small).

- Irene
Senior SRE, Redwood Operations
Attachment: rb_infra_dump_20270807.tar.gz

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Chris Mercer <chris.mercer@vaultbank.com>, procurement@vaultbank.com, sara.perez@vaultbank.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, irene_choi@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-07T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Persistent latency + 5xx during peak - reserved throughput shortfall

Chris / VaultBank team — thank you for the quick heads-up and patience. Short update and actions we've taken (internal -> external summary):

What happened: our telemetry shows an internal canary workload briefly consumed slots in the dedicated GPU pool coincident with your peak, pushing your reserved headroom to the ceiling and causing queueing and some 5xx. This is a mis-tagging + scheduling gap on our side. We're treating this as an operational failure.

Immediate mitigations performed (completed):
- Evicted non-customer canaries and paused preemptible workloads (completed 09:50 PDT).
- Applied a transient routing fallback routing 25% of traffic to a compatible quantized model variant (active now) — expected p95 improvement for routed requests: ~300-500ms.
- Enabled KV-prefix caching for high-repeat prefixes where applicable (in progress; expected complete within 45m).

Short-term relief we are providing:
- We approved a complimentary 2-hour burst on our emergency fund to cover the remainder of today's peak window. No PO required to use this immediate burst; procurement can choose to formalize afterward.
- Redwood will issue a 10% goodwill credit on your next invoice for the month.

Next steps:
- Karthik/Irene will post a short technical RCA within 48 hours and an action plan to prevent mis-tagged canaries from impacting dedicated pools.
- We'll schedule a 30-minute postmortem with vaultbank SREs and our ops/sales leads tomorrow to walk the RCA and long-term remediation (policy/routing fixes + alerting).

Attached are the customer graph and our infra dump for your review. I will remain point for coordination. If you prefer an immediate call, we can get one scheduled in the next 30 minutes.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we're treating this with high priority.

- Naomi Feldman
VP, Account Ops, Redwood Inference
Attachments: vaultbank_latency_graph.png, rb_infra_dump_20270807.tar.gz
